scope: Complete the seed-sensitivity and URL-probe methods already listed in secondary-analysis-v1. These details were chosen after development results were known. They are secondary analyses, not new confirmatory tests or changes to the primary study. Research execution requires a separately reviewed binding and runner; the in-memory helpers alone do not authenticate data or authorize a run.

seeds.training_runtime: Use the bound Python 3.10.19, PyTorch 2.7.1 float32 MPS and scipy-openblas runtime on the declared machine. Set one numerical thread, deterministic algorithms in error mode, no autocast, no MPS fallback or fast math. Record the observed runtime for each fit. Architecture, initialization, weighted BCE, AdamW, clipping and data order remain those in rq1-transformer-cascade-v2.
seeds.rng: Seed Python, NumPy, PyTorch and the training DataLoader generator with the member's declared seed before model construction. Advance generator state across epochs; never reseed at each epoch or alter the primary seed-42 entry.
seeds.checkpoint_rule: Preserve the original first-epoch checkpoint and strict later AP > recorded_best + 0.0001 rule, with patience five and maximum forty epochs. Checkpoint AP still uses validation batches of 512. Save each epoch's ordered validation probabilities and AP/loss aggregate, and each qualifying best state, before later epochs or checks. Save restored-best state before its final rescoring/AP check. Callback failures stop the attempt. Do not replace the original checkpoint rule with singleton AP.

calibration.procedure: Score the same validation rows in their original order with singleton authoritative stage-one inference and singleton float32 transformer inference for every weight set, including accepted seed 42. Keep the original stage-one cutoff and report its current counts, without claiming it was re-optimized under singleton arithmetic. Select each transformer's cutoff using the unchanged baselines-v2 CP rule, then its band using the original inclusive-distance sweep: fewest invocations, then smallest width. Preserve target_not_met if no candidate meets the gates. These validation-selected points are secondary and never replace the primary artifacts.
calibration.scoring_outputs: Retain ordered IDs, labels, stage-one and per-seed transformer probabilities, decisions, every epoch's batch-512 validation probabilities and AP used for checkpoint selection, selected thresholds/bands and logical cascade masks. Bind every record to its seed, input and fitted-weight hashes. No probability recalibration.

seeds.interpretation: Report all five weight sets and every stopped or unattempted member, without selecting the best. The historical seed-42 fit used its recorded earlier runtime; future fits use execution-v2. Common secondary scoring/calibration does not remove that training-runtime difference. Describe this as a seed/runtime sensitivity check, not an isolated causal random-seed effect.

probes.allocation: Reuse the original label-blind GMM validation domain allocation. Select audit rows without reordering; record their zero-based positions in the full validation partition. The original and each transformed stream have identical IDs and positions. Calibration rows never enter this replay.
probes.scoring: Use original primary operating points and singleton detector scores. Build monitor vectors from the 25 raw-URL features and the separate portable Logistic-L1 probability. Reuse the accepted GMM scaler with subtract-then-divide arithmetic. GMM uses its original NLL window score; MMD and PSI use accepted training references and calibration boundaries. Alerts use strict score > boundary. GMM routing changes only later requests under the existing policy. All paired scores are computed offline; masks do not measure avoided inference.
probes.retained_outputs: Save each original/output URL pair, operator, eligibility, changed flag, original ID/validation position, one-based stream position, detector scores/decisions, features, portable monitor probability, NLL, routing flags and complete monitor windows. Retain all 26 PSI feature scores. Public summaries contain only aggregate values and private-byte hashes; no URLs, row IDs or domains.

comparisons.summaries: Report row, eligible, changed, eligible-no-op and ineligible counts. For each detector, report paired decision transitions and score-change count, mean signed delta, mean absolute delta and maximum absolute delta. Apply the same paired summaries to aligned monitor window scores/alerts, with original/transformed alert counts and all window denominators.
comparisons.unavailable_monitor: Preserve the accepted reference/calibration reason, with null comparison values. Never substitute a fitted replacement or silently omit a declared monitor.

probes.interpretation: These paired changes describe sensitivity to three fixed URL-string operations. Transformed strings have no verified phishing outcome labels. No correctness, AP, recall, adversarial-success rate or replacement primary H2 decision is computed.

execution.acceptance: Bind the reviewed clean producer revision, unchanged runtime, this supplement, source/partition identities and accepted model/reference bytes before research reads. Reserve each attempt before work. Persist fitted states and intermediate outputs before later checks, record actual worker exits and safe failed-check IDs, and independently verify saved evidence before publication. A stopped fit or replay remains stopped, with its unattempted tail listed. This methods record is not an execution permission switch.
